correctness.rationale: The greedy longest-matched-prefix state q_i can rise by at most one on a new antichain level. It rises exactly when the next required alternating bit is present; for level i an increment occurs for precisely 2^{n_i}-1 colorings and no increment for exactly one. Every coloring has a unique set I of increment levels, giving product weights and the elementary-symmetric sum. Boundary h=0, k>=h and normalization to 2^{sum n_i} follow. Independently enumerated 89 level-size profiles with 1..8 vertices, computing actual longest alternating chains and comparing all coefficients; all passed. Finite checks are corroboration, not proof of the unrestricted theorem.
residual_risks: Poset formula requires complete comparability between distinct antichain levels and incomparability within each level; neither arbitrary graded posets nor both-starting-bit alternation are covered.
